finalText:
**Merge keeps history as it happened. Rebase rewrites it to look tidy.**

A merge joins two branches with one new commit. Both lines of work stay visible.

A rebase lifts your commits off and replays them on top of the other branch. You get a straight line, but those commits are copies with new IDs.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Merge
    A1[main] --> M[merge commit]
    B1[your branch] --> M
  end
  subgraph Rebase
    A2[main] --> C1[copy of commit 1] --> C2[copy of commit 2]
  end
```

Reach for rebase on your own branch, before anyone else has it. Reach for merge when the branch is shared.

The one hard rule: never rebase commits someone else already pulled. Their copy and yours stop matching.
